regulated_notice: Operational diagnostic only — not a clinical or compliance determination. Clinical triage and scheduling escalation rules must remain under authorised clinical supervision. Do not include patient names or health details.
short_description: Manage appointment requests, visit-type triage rules, pre-visit forms, confirmations, and rescheduling.

questions.question: Which channels are used for appointment requests?
What minimum information is collected to identify the patient and appointment type?
questions.placeholder: e.g. Visit reason category, new vs returning status, preferred practitioner, coverage type...
questions.privacyNote: Describe categories only — never enter real patient details.

questions.question: Who determines the appropriate appointment slot or clinician, and what rules guide that decision?
options: Reception follows written clinic visit-type & clinician matching rules
Reception asks clinician or practice nurse when unsure
Receptionist uses personal experience without written guide

questions.question: How are urgency or special scheduling needs escalated to qualified staff?
questions.placeholder: e.g. Red-flag symptoms flagged to triage nurse immediately per clinic protocol...

questions.question: How is the booking recorded and confirmed to the patient?
options: Booked in clinic EHR/practice system with automated SMS/email confirmation
Entered in calendar and confirmed manually by reception

questions.question: What preparation, forms or records are needed before arrival?
questions.placeholder: e.g. Intake/consent form, prior referral summary, fasting/prep instructions...

questions.question: How are cancellations, rescheduling and no-shows handled and tracked?
questions.placeholder: e.g. Waitlist checked manually if someone cancels; no-shows noted in EHR...

regulated_notice: Operational diagnostic only — not a clinical or compliance determination. Clinical assessment and identity verification policies remain under authorised clinic leadership. Do not enter patient data.
short_description: Verify arriving patients, collect consent/intake updates, notify clinical staff, and record rooming status.

questions.question: What steps happen when a patient arrives?
questions.placeholder: e.g. Checks in at desk or kiosk, confirms appointment, waits in reception...

questions.question: How is identity confirmed using the clinic's approved procedure?
options: Two-identifier check by receptionist per clinic policy

questions.question: What demographic, consent, coverage or administrative information is checked or updated?
How does reception notify clinical staff that the patient is ready?
options: Status changed in clinic system visible in clinical room
Internal chat message or intercom/walk down hallway
Paper chart placed in physical tray

questions.question: What information is handed to the clinical team and through which approved channel?
questions.placeholder: e.g. Completed intake packet scanned into EHR before medical assistant rooms patient...

questions.question: How are late arrivals, missing records or urgent concerns handled?
questions.placeholder: e.g. Reception checks with clinician whether to squeeze in or reschedule...

questions.question: Where is check-in completion recorded and who can see patient status?
options: Live status board inside EHR visible to front desk and clinical team
Reception knows; clinicians have to ask or check waiting room

regulated_notice: Operational diagnostic only — clinical triage and referral urgency must remain with qualified clinicians. Do not include patient health information.
short_description: Log inbound referrals, check completeness, support clinician triage, book visits, and close the loop with referrers.

questions.question: How are referrals received and logged?
What information must accompany a referral before it can be reviewed?
questions.placeholder: e.g. Referring clinician details, clinical history summary, recent imaging/labs...

questions.question: Who performs clinical triage or determines urgency?
options: Designated triage clinician / specialist reviews every referral
Nurse screens using written clinical criteria
Admin guesses urgency unless marked Urgent on cover

questions.question: How are incomplete referrals returned or clarified?
questions.placeholder: e.g. Coordinator faxes/emails referrer office and puts referral in pending folder...

questions.question: Who owns contacting the patient and arranging the appointment?
questions.placeholder: e.g. Referral coordinator calls patient up to 3 times...

questions.question: How do you track referrals that are not booked, declined or not attended?
options: Central referral queue with overdue alerts
No reliable tracking once message is left

questions.question: How is the outcome communicated to the referring clinician through approved channels?
questions.placeholder: e.g. Consultation letter faxed or sent via secure EHR message after visit...

regulated_notice: Operational diagnostic only — interpretation of test results and clinical communication decisions must always be made by authorised clinicians.
short_description: Match inbound lab/imaging results, ensure clinician review, handle urgent escalations, and verify loop closure.

questions.question: How are results received and matched to the correct patient record?
options: Electronic lab interface matches into EHR automatically
Admin downloads PDFs/faxes and attaches manually to patient chart

questions.question: Who is responsible for ensuring each result is reviewed?
questions.placeholder: e.g. Ordering clinician signs off in inbox; practice nurse monitors overdue queue if clinician is away...

questions.question: How are urgent or abnormal results escalated under clinic policy?
questions.placeholder: e.g. Lab phones clinic directly for critical values; handed immediately to duty doctor...

questions.question: Who decides what clinical action or communication is appropriate?
options: Ordering or covering clinician makes all clinical decisions
Clinician sets action note for nurse/admin to deliver approved message

questions.question: How is the patient contacted and how is successful communication confirmed?
questions.placeholder: e.g. Secure portal message, phone call, or follow-up booking logged in chart...

questions.question: How are failed contact attempts and outstanding actions tracked?
options: Tracked task list with escalation rule after X missed attempts
Notes in patient chart without an active follow-up queue

questions.question: How does the clinic verify that no result remains unreviewed or uncommunicated?
questions.placeholder: e.g. Weekly reconciliation of ordered tests vs received & signed-off results...
